Consider the ellipse $E$ and the vector field $F,$ shown above. Let $C$ be any path where $E$ is traversed once in the counterclockwise direction. Which of the following statements are true?

- ${∮}_{-C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0$
- ${∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0$
- ${∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r=0$

Consider the circle $S$ and vector field $F$ shown above. Let $C$ be any path where $S$ is traversed once in the counterclockwise direction. Which of the following statements are true?

- ${∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0$
- ${∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r=0$
- ${∮}_{-C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0$
feedback.worked_solution:
The circulation $Γ$ measures the total work done by a force $F$ in moving a particle along a *closed* curve $C.$
It is given by the formula

$$
Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

We now recall the following:

- If the force works *with* the motion of the particle (i.e., the force helps to push the particle along the path), then ${∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0.$

- If the force works *against* the motion of the particle (i.e., the force impedes the motion of the particle as it moves along the path), then ${∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0.$

With that in mind, let's check each statement.

- Statement I is false, while statement II is true. Since the force $F$ acts perpendicular to the motion of the particle as it moves around $C,$ it neither helps nor hinders its motion. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14060266/assets/eb4da8143700c7d31e0ceacd09ac76a8d1bcb10379a34dce5b59d48f2ae58c13.png)

So, ${∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r=0.$

- Statement III is false. If we reverse the orientation of $C,$ then the situation with regards to the work done by $F$ remains unchanged.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14060266/assets/70a473397216589350f63482ab3e36cb1247e7825046c70642254c8514564b00.png)

So, ${∮}_{-C}F\cdot \text{d}r=0.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."
